solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dated a right Charlie drinking spicy drink

indicators.note: a drinker takes liquid inside, so the drink's letters go within the others

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the usual abbreviation for right
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
chai is spiced Indian tea

explanation.surface: Someone recalls going out with a real fool who was sipping a spiced drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dated' reads as a verb about a romance, but it is the adjective meaning old-fashioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Something archaic is antiquated, belonging to an earlier era, which is what dated means as an adjective.

clue.text: Dynamic fourth part of staged work has energy

blocks.note: the fourth section of a play is Act IV, written in Roman numerals
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A critic praises the lively fourth act of a theatre production for its energy.
explanation.walkthrough: Plays divide into acts numbered in Roman numerals, so the fourth is ACT IV.
explanation.definitionFit: Dynamic and active are synonyms, both describing someone or something full of vigour and movement.

clue.text: Succeeded in accurate working in class

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it, so a letter goes into the middle of the other letters
working suggests the letters are set in motion and rearranged into a new order

blocks.note: s. is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies
the anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone did well at precise work during a lesson at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Class' sounds like a school lesson but is the biological rank: crabs, lobsters and shrimps form the class Crustacea.
explanation.definitionFit: Crustacea is a taxonomic class of arthropods, so it is literally a class in biological classification.

clue.text: Hoping to offload Samsung's ultimate tablet

indicators.note: offloading something means getting rid of it, so a letter is dropped from the word
'ultimate' keeps only the last letter of 'Samsung'

blocks.note: aspiring means hoping or aiming for something
the final letter of the brand name

explanation.surface: Someone hopes to sell off a Samsung tablet computer, its latest model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tablet' and 'Samsung' paint a computer, but the tablet is a pill; 'ultimate' means last letter, not latest model.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspirin is a common painkiller usually taken as a pill, and a tablet is a compressed pill.

clue.text: Vessel in southern English river with article that's tin-plated

indicators.note: something plated is coated all over, so the outer word wraps round the rest

blocks.note: the Tamar runs through southwest England between Devon and Cornwall
the indefinite article
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A boat on a river in the south of England carries a metal-coated item.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tamar forms most of the border between Devon and Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: A catamaran is a boat with two parallel hulls, and vessel is a general word for a boat or ship.

clue.text: Man, say, that is filling glasses

indicators.note: a filling goes inside something, so these letters sit within the other word

blocks.note: specs is short for spectacles
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A man, for instance, whose eyes are filling his spectacles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' means humankind here, not a male person; 'say' marks it as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Humankind, Homo sapiens, is one example of a biological species, so 'say' signals an instance.

clue.text: Child beginning to suck a kind of rock

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: opening letter of suck
prog is progressive rock, a musical genre

explanation.surface: A child starts to suck on a lump of stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' looks like stone but is music: prog rock. Sprog is British slang for a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprog is informal British slang for a young child or baby, a playful equivalent of kid.

clue.text: No one except revolutionary is sidestepping the issue

indicators.note: a revolution turns things right round, so the preceding words are read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one
save means except, as in 'all save one'

explanation.surface: Nobody but a revolutionary is dodging the real question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a person, but it turns NO, I and SAVE back to front together.
explanation.definitionFit: Evasion is the act of avoiding a question or duty, which is exactly dodging the point at hand.

clue.text: Very old Brits chill, turning up at home

indicators.note: in a down clue turning something upward makes it read from bottom to top, so backwards

blocks.note: to ice something is to chill it
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: Elderly British people relax after showing up at someone's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very old' means ancient, not elderly: the Iceni were the tribe of Boudicca in Roman Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were a Celtic tribe of ancient eastern Britain, so they are Britons from very long ago.

clue.text: Determined to hold golf club up before a miss

indicators.note: to hold something is to have it inside, so the first word wraps round the next
in a down clue going up means reading from the bottom, so the word is backwards

blocks.note: set on something means determined
an iron is a type of golf club
taken as written

explanation.surface: A golfer, set on keeping the club raised, takes a swing that misses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' suggests a failed shot, but it is a title for a young unmarried woman, which is what the Spanish word means.
explanation.definitionFit: Señorita is the Spanish form of address for an unmarried young woman, the equivalent of the English 'Miss'.

clue.text: Musician's funny Christian rock after tango

indicators.note: after places the piece it follows second, so the opening phonetic letter comes before the funny word

blocks.note: tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet
rum means odd or strange
Jesus named the apostle Peter the rock on which he would build his church

explanation.surface: A musician's oddball Christian rock band, which follows a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Musician's' stands for 'musician is', so it can be the definition. 'Christian rock' sounds like a genre; it is Peter, whose name means rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A trumpeter is a musician who plays the trumpet; the 's here is short for 'is'.

clue.text: Having peeled date, a German did duck meals outside

indicators.note: peeling removes the outer skin, so the first and last letters go and the middle stays

blocks.note: the inside of the word with its outer letters stripped
ein is German for a

explanation.surface: After stripping a fruit, someone from Germany dodged eating out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' is a verb, to avoid, not the bird on the menu; to duck meals outside is to eat at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Ate in means had a meal at home, which is the opposite of dining out, so it avoided eating outside.

clue.text: One putting a cross in the box in footie, regularly caught by vacuous viewer

definitions.text: One putting a cross in the box

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
something caught is held inside, so these letters go within the next word
vacuous means empty, so the inside of the word is removed and only its ends remain

blocks.note: the first and last letters with the inside emptied out
second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A footballer crosses into the penalty box, watched by a bored spectator.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'cross in the box' is football talk in the surface, but means marking a ballot paper. Footie is British slang for football.
explanation.definitionFit: A voter marks an X in the box beside a candidate's name on a ballot paper.

clue.text: One blowing up foe finally, if arming bombs

indicators.note: finally points to the end of the word, so only its closing letter is kept
bombs blow things apart, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

blocks.note: the closing letter of foe
the rest of the anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: An explosives expert destroys the enemy at last, if the bombs are armed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blowing up' suggests explosion but means enlarging, as a magnifying glass does.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnifier enlarges the apparent size of things, and to blow up an image is to enlarge it.

clue.text: Smuggler in Berlin is following group of Nicaraguan rebels

indicators.note: following means coming behind, so the German word is placed after the rebel group

blocks.note: the Contras were Nicaraguan rebels, and a band is a group
ist is German for is

explanation.surface: A smuggler operating in Berlin trails a band of Central American guerrillas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' puts the German word after the rebel group; 'in Berlin' tells you to translate into German.
explanation.definitionFit: A contrabandist deals in contraband, goods imported or exported illegally, so he is a smuggler.

clue.text: Playing jazz live and dancing

blocks.note: to be is to exist or live
bopping is informal for dancing to pop music

explanation.surface: Performing jazz on stage and dancing along to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live' sounds like a live performance, but it is the verb meaning exist.
explanation.definitionFit: Bebop is a fast, complex style of jazz, so bebopping means playing in that style.

clue.text: Popular ruler wants time, one signalling change of direction

indicators.note: to want something can mean to lack it, so a letter is missing from the word

blocks.note: something in is fashionable or popular
a dictator is an absolute ruler
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A well-liked ruler needs time for one who signals a change of policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wants' looks like desire but means lacks, so one T leaves the ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's indicator is the flashing light that tells other drivers it is about to turn.

clue.text: Old island-hopper uses elastic after trunk's losing lid

indicators.note: elastic material stretches out of shape, so the letters are bent into a new order
a lid sits on top, so losing it takes away the opening letter

blocks.note: the trunk is the body, plus the possessive s
anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: An elderly traveller between islands uses a bungee cord after his luggage loses its top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunk' suggests luggage but is the torso; Homer's hero spent ten years sailing between Mediterranean islands after Troy.
explanation.definitionFit: Odysseus, Homer's ancient Greek hero, wandered from island to island on his long voyage home.

clue.text: Drunk in bar did groan, drying out here

indicators.note: a drunk person staggers about, so the letters are jumbled out of order

blocks.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A drunk in a pub groaned while sobering up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drying out' sounds like recovering from drink, but it is about wet dishes left to dry by the sink.
explanation.definitionFit: A draining board is the grooved surface beside a kitchen sink where washed dishes are left to dry.

clue.text: Door staff turned handle here

indicators.note: something turned round faces the other way, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: a gateman guards an entrance

explanation.surface: The doormen twisted the handle at this spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handle' looks like a door handle, but it is slang for a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Handle is slang for a person's name, and a name tag is a label where your name is displayed.

clue.text: Continental area — cool hedges endlessly fertile

indicators.note: a hedge surrounds a field, so the word encloses what follows
without an end means the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for area
to fan is to cool
rich soil is fertile

explanation.surface: A European region where cool hedgerows are endlessly fertile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Continental' suggests mainland Europe to a British reader, but here it means belonging to any continent, Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: African describes something from Africa, one of the world's continents, so it is a continental adjective.

clue.text: Picked up soldier's rank meat

indicators.note: picked up as in heard, so the word is identified by its spoken sound

blocks.note: a colonel is a senior army officer, pronounced like the answer

explanation.surface: A soldier collected his officer's rank-smelling meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Meat here is the edible part of a nut, as in the meat of a walnut, not flesh.
explanation.definitionFit: A kernel is the edible inner part of a nut or seed, which is also called its meat.

clue.text: Outraged sons formed an alliance

blocks.note: s is the abbreviation for son or sons
to team up is to join forces

explanation.surface: Furious brothers joined together against their parents.
explanation.walkthrough: Steamed up is informal for angry, as if steam were coming out of the ears.
explanation.definitionFit: Being steamed up means being very angry or agitated, an idiom close in meaning to outraged.

clue.text: Howler monkey losing its head

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so that letter goes

blocks.note: a little monkey, a mischievous child, is a little terror

explanation.surface: A howler monkey is decapitated.
explanation.walkthrough: The howler monkey is a real species, so the eye reads the two words together; split them: 'Howler' is a blunder, 'monkey' a naughty child.
explanation.definitionFit: A howler is a glaring, laughable mistake, so it is a type of mistake.

clue.text: Perhaps like hummus and nuts

blocks.note: first meaning: resembling a dip, as hummus is an example of one
second meaning: crazy or scatterbrained

explanation.surface: A description of a snack platter of hummus and nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' sits naturally beside hummus as food, but it means crazy. 'Perhaps' warns that hummus is just one example of a dip.
explanation.definitionFit: Dippy is informal for foolish or crazy, and jokingly also suits something dip-like, as hummus is a dip.

clue.text: Scouting leaders in cub expeditions on playing field

indicators.note: the leaders are the words' front-runners, so their opening letters are taken
in an across clue one thing on another sits after it, so the selected letters follow the playing field

blocks.note: rec is short for recreation ground, a public playing field
the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Cub Scout leaders take their troop on outings to the sports field.
explanation.walkthrough: Recce is British military slang for reconnaissance; 'on' allows the letters to follow REC in an across clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A recce is a reconnaissance, an act of scouting out an area before going in.

clue.text: One seen wading in say river banks in Egypt

indicators.note: the banks of a river are its two edges, so only the outer letters are kept

blocks.note: e.g. means for example, or say
R is the abbreviation for river
first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone spotted paddling along the banks of the Nile in Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a white heron that stands and wades in shallow water to catch fish.

clue.text: Good deal on cost drawing in new students here

indicators.note: drawing something in pulls it inside, so a letter is placed within the word

blocks.note: price and cost are synonyms
N is the abbreviation for new
a ton is informal for a large amount, a good deal

explanation.surface: A bargain on fees attracts fresh students to this university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good deal' sounds like a bargain but means a lot, a ton; 'on' puts it after the price in an across clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Princeton is a prestigious Ivy League university in New Jersey, so it is a place where students study.

clue.text: Star's face — rugged and thin

indicators.note: a face is the front of something, so the opening letter is used

blocks.note: the opening letter
craggy means rugged, like a weathered face

explanation.surface: A film star's face is weathered and lean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rugged and thin' looks like two descriptions of the face, but only 'thin' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Scraggy means scrawny or lean and bony, so it is a near-synonym of thin.

clue.text: Try playing in Lear, wanting a role therein

indicators.note: playing about with something moves it around, so the letters change places
wanting here means lacking, so the named letter is taken out of the fodder

blocks.note: a go is an attempt or try
anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor tries performing in King Lear, hoping for a part in the play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Therein' points back to Lear, the play whose title also supplies most of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Goneril is King Lear's eldest daughter in Shakespeare's tragedy, so she is a character in that play.
